title: Issue of Debentures
summary: Debentures are written acknowledgements of debt issued by a company to raise long-term borrowed funds. This chapter covers their types, issue at par, premium and discount, issue for consideration other than cash and as collateral security, the six cases of issue with terms of redemption, interest, and writing off the discount or loss on issue.

notes.heading: Meaning, features and types
notes.html:
A debenture is a document issued under the company's seal acknowledging a debt, carrying a fixed rate of interest and repayable after a specified period. Section 2(30) of the Companies Act, 2013 includes debenture stock, bonds and other instruments evidencing a debt.

BasisTypes
SecuritySecured (mortgage), Unsecured (naked)
RedemptionRedeemable, Irredeemable (perpetual)
ConvertibilityConvertible (fully/partly), Non-convertible

notes.heading: Issue for cash: par, premium, discount
notes.html:
Debentures of ₹100 each may be issued at par (₹100), at a premium (above ₹100) or at a discount (below ₹100). Unlike shares, debentures can be issued at a discount.

notes.heading: Issue for consideration other than cash
notes.html:
When assets or a business are purchased and the vendor is paid in debentures:

  1. Sundry Assets A/c Dr. (agreed value); Goodwill A/c Dr. (if purchase consideration exceeds net assets); To Sundry Liabilities A/c; To Vendor A/c; To Capital Reserve A/c (if net assets exceed purchase consideration).
  2. Vendor A/c Dr.; To % Debentures A/c; To Securities Premium A/c (if at premium). If at discount, Discount on Issue of Debentures A/c is debited.

Number of debentures = Purchase consideration ÷ Issue price.

Illustration 1

X Ltd. took over assets of ₹5,00,000 and liabilities of ₹60,000 of Y Ltd. for ₹4,95,000, paid by issue of 10% debentures of ₹100 each at a premium of 10%.

Net assets = ₹4,40,000, so Goodwill = 4,95,000 − 4,40,000 = ₹55,000. Debentures issued = 4,95,000 ÷ 110 = 4,500.

notes.heading: Issue as collateral security
notes.html:
Debentures given to a lender as additional (secondary) security for a loan. No interest is paid on them; the lender can sell or keep them only if the company defaults.

  • Method 1: no journal entry; the fact is disclosed in the note on borrowings.
  • Method 2: Debenture Suspense A/c Dr. To % Debentures A/c. In the Balance Sheet, Debenture Suspense is deducted from Debentures in the note. The entry is reversed when the loan is repaid.

notes.heading: Interest and writing off discount or loss
notes.html:
• Interest is calculated on the face value at the fixed rate, whether or not the company earns a profit. It is a charge against profit.
  • Entries: Debenture Interest A/c Dr. To Debentureholders A/c (due); Debentureholders A/c Dr. To Bank A/c (paid); Statement of Profit and Loss Dr. To Debenture Interest A/c (transfer, shown under Finance Costs).
  • Discount/Loss on Issue of Debentures is a capital loss. It is written off in the year of issue, first from Securities Premium (Section 52(2)) and the balance, if any, from the Statement of Profit and Loss as a finance cost.

Entry: Securities Premium A/c Dr.; Statement of Profit and Loss Dr.; To Discount/Loss on Issue of Debentures A/c.

Common mistakes: computing interest on issue price instead of face value; crediting Securities Premium when the premium is on redemption; forgetting that collateral debentures carry no interest.

Excess of face value over issue price; a capital loss.
Total of discount on issue and premium payable on redemption, recorded at the time of issue.

mcqs.q: Debentureholders are the ______ of a company.
mcqs.explanation: Debentures are borrowed funds, so the holders are lenders, that is creditors.

mcqs.q: 500, 10% debentures of ₹100 each are issued at par, redeemable at 5% premium. Loss on Issue of Debentures is
mcqs.explanation: Premium on redemption = 500 × ₹5 = ₹2,500, recorded as loss on issue.

mcqs.explanation: It is an amount payable to debentureholders, hence a liability.

mcqs.q: Discount on issue of debentures is written off first from
mcqs.explanation: Section 52(2) permits Securities Premium to be used; only the balance goes to the Statement of Profit and Loss.

mcqs.q:
Assertion (A): Interest on debentures is paid even if the company incurs a loss.
Reason (R): Interest on debentures is a charge against profit.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Being a charge (not an appropriation), interest is payable regardless of profit.

questions.q: What is meant by issue of debentures as collateral security?
questions.answerHtml: It means issuing debentures to a lender as additional security for a loan, over and above the primary security. The lender has a right over them only if the company fails to repay the loan.

questions.q: Give three differences between a share and a debenture.
questions.answerHtml:
• Status: a shareholder is an owner; a debentureholder is a creditor.
  • Return: dividend on shares is paid out of profits and may vary; interest on debentures is fixed and payable even in a loss.
  • Voting rights: shareholders have voting rights; debentureholders do not.
